newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY-FLYERS FIRE COACH TERRY MURRAY SIX DAYS AFTER CUP SWEEP.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY-FLYERS FIRE COACH TERRY MURRAY SIX DAYS AFTER CUP SWEEP.

text.p: Finishing second best was not enough to save the job of Philadelphia Flyers coach Terry Murray, who was fired Friday, less than a week after his team was swept by Detroit in the Stanley Cup finals.
Murray guided the Flyers to their first appearance in the finals in a decade, but a poor relationship with his players apparently cost the coach his job.
"The problems that existed between the coach and the players were problems that I did not feel could be fixed," said Flyers general manager Bobby Clarke, who did not name a replacement for Murray.
"It's unfortunate that we had to take such a drastic step, but I felt it was necessary in order for the team to move forward."

The 46-year-old Murray was criticised for flip-flopping his goaltenders during the playoffs, rather than sticking with either Ron Hextall or Garth Snow. And he may have done himself irreparable damage by suggesting his team was choking after going down 0-3 in the finals against Detroit.
But failing to win the support of the team's young superstar captain, Eric Lindros, may be what finally pushed him out the door.
"It's not a decision that the players had any involvement in," Clarke insisted. "We have an organisation and I talk to people in the organisation that I trust. But the ultimate decision was mine."
The Flyers went 45-24-13 this season -- their third under Murray -- and finished second to New Jersey in the Atlantic Division with 103 points, fourth overall in the NHL.

The Flyers went on to wipe out Pittsburgh, Buffalo and the New York Rangers in five games each in the first three rounds of the playoffs. But the team appeared in disarray against the Red Wings in the Stanley Cup championship series.
Murray compiled a 118-64-30 record in his three seasons with the Flyers, and his 28 playoff victories places him third on the club's all-time list behind Fred Shero and Mike Keenan.
The Flyers, who last won the Stanley Cup in 1975 under Shero, are the eighth NHL team to change head coaches since the end of the regular season.
